title: Tracing pottery use and the emergence of secondary product exploitation through lipid residue analysis at Late Neolithic Tell Sabi Abyad (Syria)
version: Journal of Archaeological Science 64, pp. 54–66, doi:10.1016/j.jas.2015.10.002.
lineage: Original vessel lipid assays, distinct from the stratigraphic study of earliest pottery and from faunal observations. Evershed et al. 2008 and the 2018 chapter partly report this same sample series.

passages.note: Sample SAB263 from Operation IV, Grey Burnished Ware, has a ruminant dairy signature in a ca. 6400–6330 cal BCE context. Samples SAB2 and SAB173 from Dark-Faced Burnished Ware and SAB214 from Standard Fine Ware are assigned ruminant dairy in contexts dated ca. 6000–5900 cal BCE.

The specific animal species and milk products cannot be inferred. The study compares the sherd evidence with independently observed faunal age profiles. The authors report later mixed meat and secondary-product exploitation as a plausible interpretation.
